subject: Execution geography, transient hops, and deletion guarantees
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@healthcore.com>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick clarification on where request execution happens and deletion controls

Vanessa,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — good stuff. Before we move this forward with procurement, our security team needs a short Q&A about where customer request processing actually occurs and what happens when we ask for deletion. A few specific asks: 

1) For Redwood Hosted API calls from US customers, where can we expect the inference execution to run (region/hops)? Are there transient handoffs to third-party clouds or edge providers?
2) Which subprocessors might touch request payloads (tokenization, logging, telemetry) — can you provide a roster or example categories?
3) If a user asks for deletion, what is the timeline for removing live cache, KV entries, logs, and backups? Any retention windows we should assume?

We just need concise, actionable answers we can include in our security assessment. Attachments are fine.

Appreciate it,
Alex Morgan
Security Lead — HealthCore Labs

From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@healthcore.com>
Cc: jordan_blake@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-05-09T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarification on where request execution happens and deletion controls

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. Below are concise answers you can drop into your assessment. I attached a simplified data flow diagram and our current subprocessor roster for context. Short version first; details after.

1) Execution geography and transient hops - Hosted API: Primary execution happens in the customer-selected region (we currently offer us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1). For US customers default is us-west-2 unless you pin another region.
- Transient hops: Requests are routed through our control plane (control-plane metadata only) and then to the execution pool. Payloads do not persist in the control plane. Transient network hops are limited to: our routing gateway (region edge), the execution host, and, rarely, a caching layer in the same region. We do not route inference payloads through third-party edge providers by default.
- Cross-border fallback: If capacity in the pinned region is exhausted and you have not locked region enforcement, traffic may be routed to a compatible execution pool in a nearby region (e.g., us-east-1) — we will not route to EU/APAC unless you opt into cross-region fallback.

2) Subprocessors that may touch payloads (examples/categorization) - Compute providers (GPU hosts): managed infra partners that host execution pools. All are covered by our DPA and subprocess agreements.
- Logging/telemetry vendors: aggregated request telemetry (latency, errors) flows to our metrics backend; raw payloads are not stored in telemetry streams.
- Observability/storage: short-lived KV caches and perf caches live on execution hosts; persistent logs are stored in encrypted object storage for a limited retention window.

3) Deletion guarantees and timelines (hosted mode)
- Live KV/cache eviction: immediate upon request — in-line caches and KV entries for a customer are evicted during the delete operation (typically within seconds to a few minutes).
- Short-lived logs and telemetry: scrubbed within 48 hours after the request if marked for deletion; operational traces that include identifiers are redacted and tombstoned.
- Persistent backups / snapshots: we maintain immutable snapshots for resilience with a maximum retention of 30 days (configurable under Dedicated/Private contracts). Backups are subject to the 30-day purge schedule unless you require shorter retention via contract.

Notes: Dedicated and Private deployments have stronger guarantees (region pinning, optional on-prem packaging, and custom deletion SLAs). If region locking is a hard requirement for HealthCore, we recommend Dedicated or Private so we can sign that into the contract.

Attachments: redwood_data_flow_v2.pdf, subprocessor_roster_2029-04.csv

If helpful, Jordan and Marissa are looping on follow-ups below.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@healthcore.com>

Subject: Re: Quick clarification on where request execution happens and deletion controls

Vanessa —

This is really helpful, thanks. A couple quick clarifications so procurement can finalize the SOW: 

• When you say "control plane" only handles metadata, can you confirm no request payload is written to long-term control-plane logs?
• For the 30-day backup retention, is there an option to elect a 7-day or 0-day backup window as part of the Dedicated contract?

If you can answer those two lines we can roll this into the assessment and move to signatures.

—Alex

From: jordan_blake@redwood.ai
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@healthcore.com>, procurement@healthcore.com
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2029-05-10T15:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick clarification on where request execution happens and deletion controls

Alex — looping in short answers so procurement has the exact language for the SOW.

1) Control plane logs: Confirmed — the control plane processes routing metadata and does not persist customer request payloads to long-term logs. Operational control-plane logs may include routing IDs and non-content metadata; any identifiers are redacted on deletion requests.

2) Backup retention options: For Dedicated contracts we can offer configurable snapshot retention. Standard hosted customers default to a 30-day immutable snapshot window; Dedicated customers can choose 7-day, 14-day, or 0-day snapshot policies in the contract. Setting 0-day requires a technical onboarding checklist (we disable automatic snapshots and require agreed operational playbooks).

If HealthCore wants region-lock guarantees and 0/7-day backup, Marissa and I can draft the contract language and a mutual action plan for the onboarding runbook.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
